records.law: For n>=1, return D1 TRUE=1 iff length(word)=2^n AND the cyclic windows word[i],...,word[(i+n-1) mod 2^n] over all starts i∈[0,2^n) are pairwise distinct (equivalently cover all 2^n possible n-bit strings exactly once). Return D1 FALSE=0 for any well-typed word failing length or uniqueness. Invalid non-D1 data or n<=0 is a domain error, never a sneaky TRUE.

positive_witnesses.why: changed bit creates duplicate cyclic n-window
extra delimiter/bit changes required exact length
empty word never has required length
primitive 01 repetition does not cover all 2-bit patterns

falsifiers: Counting only linear substrings without wrap-around rejects valid 0011 at n=2
Accepting length 2^n with duplicate n-bit windows mistakes length for universal coverage
Treating a repeated primitive block as sufficient wrongly accepts 0101 at n=2
Treating word rotations as semantically different wrongly rejects 10001011 at n=3
Using an LFSR period alone without the all-zero state can miss one n-bit window
records.distinct_from: PRIMITIVE-BINARY-WORD-ROOT: predicate checks all cyclic n-bit windows, not primitive-root decomposition
records.limitations: Source-era HOLD remains historically true; modern research selection does not grant ratification, physical code, or a proof that an evaluator primitive is necessary.

records.law: Return the unique finite factor list (l1,...,lk) such that concat(li)=w; all li are Lyndon (strictly lexicographically smaller than every proper nonempty suffix); and l1 >= l2 >= ... >= lk under explicit lexicographic 0<1. For empty source return []. No dependence on physical packing, phoneme ordering or hardware transport.
falsifiers: Returning a shortest repeated primitive root (e.g. 01010 -> 01010) instead of the ordered factor list is wrong.
Allowing increasing factors l_i<l_(i+1) violates the theorem's canonical ordering.
Factoring by a hidden phoneme collation rather than explicit D1 order 0<1 changes identity.
Treating nonempty '00' as a Lyndon component is invalid: it equals a proper suffix only lexically larger, and is not primitive.
records.distinct_from: PRIMITIVE-BINARY-WORD-ROOT: returns unique nonincreasing full Lyndon factorization, not shortest repeated root
records.limitations: Source-era HOLD remains historically true; modern research selection does not grant ratification, physical code, or a proof that an evaluator primitive is necessary.

records.law: Generate exact L/R path from root 1/1 by repeated numerator/denominator comparison and subtractive Euclid; compress maximal same-bit runs using quotient floor((a-1)/b) or floor((b-1)/a), preserving final equality stop without one extra step. Reject nonpositive and imprecise source inputs; reverse accepts ONLY alternating positive-length bit runs. Two-direction round trips are identity and representation is unique for every positive rational.

positive_witnesses.note: exact run compression from Euclid, final right run of 3
billion path steps represented by one positive run
unbounded integer width, no bit expansion

falsifiers: For 3/1, returning right-run count 3 rather than 2 introduces an extra branch past the exact rational.
For 1/1, returning any left or right step is not the root path.
For 5/2, reversing R² L into L R² reaches a different fraction.
Consecutive same-direction run records must reject rather than silently admit a noncanonical alternative code.
Zero/negative run counts, boolean bits, floats and nonpositive input rationals must reject.
A billion left steps must remain a run count, not allocate a billion-element bit sequence.
Turning the path into the nearest denominator-bounded fraction instead of exactly reversible p/q changes the mathematical meaning.
records.distinct_from: BOUNDED-RATIONAL-APPROX: lossless canonical positive fraction path rather than approximate bounded fraction
